title: Hello, World!
statement: Print the text `Hello, World!` exactly as shown.
solution: print("Hello, World!")

title: Sum of Two Numbers
statement: Read two integers and print their sum.
inputFormat: One line with two integers `a` and `b`.
solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
print(a + b)

title: Even or Odd
statement: Read an integer `n`. Print `Even` if it is even, otherwise print `Odd`.
solution:
n = int(input())

title: Largest of Three
statement: Read three integers and print the largest one.
solution: print(max(map(int, input().split())))

title: Simple Interest
statement: Read principal `P`, yearly rate `R` (percent) and time `T` in years. Print the simple interest `P * R * T / 100` with exactly two digits after the decimal point.
inputFormat: One line with three numbers `P R T`.
outputFormat: Print the interest with two decimal places.
solution:
p, r, t = map(float, input().split())
print(f"{p * r * t / 100:.2f}")

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
statement: Read a temperature in Celsius and print it in Fahrenheit using `F = C * 9 / 5 + 32`, with two decimal places.
solution:

title: Leap Year
statement: A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4 but not by 100, or if it is divisible by 400. Print `Yes` for a leap year and `No` otherwise.
solution:
y = int(input())
print("Yes" if (y % 4 == 0 and y % 100 != 0) or y % 400 == 0 else "No")

title: Factorial
statement: Print `n!` (the product `1 * 2 * ... * n`). By definition `0! = 1`.
solution:

for i in range(2, n + 1):

print(f)

title: Fibonacci Series
statement: Print the first `n` Fibonacci numbers separated by spaces. The series starts `0 1 1 2 3 ...`.
solution:

title: Prime Check
statement: Print `Prime` if `n` is a prime number, otherwise `Not Prime`. 0 and 1 are not prime.
solution:
n = int(input())
ok = n > 1
i = 2
while ok and i * i <= n:
    if n % i == 0:
        ok = False
    i += 1
print("Prime" if ok else "Not Prime")

title: Primes up to N
statement: Print all prime numbers from 2 to `n`, separated by spaces. If there are none, print an empty line.
outputFormat: Print the primes on one line.

title: GCD and LCM
statement: Read two positive integers and print their greatest common divisor and least common multiple.
solution:
a, b = map(int, input().split())
x, y = a, b
while y:
    x, y = y, x % y
print(x, a // x * b)

title: Armstrong Number
statement: An Armstrong number equals the sum of its digits each raised to the number of digits (for example `153 = 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3`). Print `Yes` or `No`.
solution:

print("Yes" if sum(int(d) ** len(s) for d in s) == int(s) else "No")

title: Remove Duplicates
statement: Remove repeated values from a list, keeping the first occurrence of each, and print the result separated by spaces.
solution:
input()
seen = set()
out = []
for x in input().split():
    if x not in seen:

        out.append(x)
print(*out)

title: Matrix Addition
statement: Add two matrices of the same size and print the result.
inputFormat: First line `r c`. Next `r` lines: matrix A. Next `r` lines: matrix B.
solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]
b = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]
for i in range(r):
    print(*[a[i][j] + b[i][j] for j in range(c)])

solution:

    print(*[m[i][j] for i in range(r)])

title: Matrix Multiplication
statement: Multiply an `n x m` matrix A by an `m x p` matrix B and print the `n x p` product.
inputFormat: First line `n m p`. Next `n` lines: A. Next `m` lines: B.
solution:
n, m, p = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
b = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]
for i in range(n):
    print(*[sum(a[i][k] * b[k][j] for k in range(m)) for j in range(p)])

title: Binary Search
statement: The list is sorted in ascending order with distinct values. Print the index (0-based) of `x`, or `-1` if it is missing. Try to use binary search.
inputFormat: First line `n`. Second line `n` sorted integers. Third line `x`.
solution:
input()
v = list(map(int, input().split()))
x = int(input())
lo, hi = 0, len(v) - 1
ans = -1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if v[mid] == x:
        ans = mid
        break
    if v[mid] < x:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(ans)

k %= n
print(*(v[-k:] + v[:-k] if k else v))

title: Most Frequent Word
statement: Find the word that occurs most often (case-insensitive, words separated by spaces). If several words tie, print the one that is alphabetically smallest. Print the word in lower case followed by its count.
solution:
from collections import Counter
c = Counter(input().lower().split())
best = min(c, key=lambda w: (-c[w], w))
print(best, c[best])

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
statement: Find the largest possible sum of a contiguous, non-empty part of the list (Kadane's algorithm).
solution:
input()
best = cur = None
for x in map(int, input().split()):
    cur = x if cur is None or cur < 0 else cur + x
    best = cur if best is None else max(best, cur)
print(best)

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement: Print the longest prefix shared by all the words. If there is none, print `-`.
inputFormat: First line `n`. Next `n` lines: one word each.
solution:
n = int(input())
ws = [input().strip() for _ in range(n)]
p = ws[0]
for w in ws[1:]:
    while not w.startswith(p):
        p = p[:-1]
print(p or '-')

title: All Subsets
statement: Print every subset of the numbers `1..n`, one per line, in lexicographic order of the numbers. Numbers inside a subset are separated by spaces and in increasing order; print the empty subset as `{}` first.
solution:
n = int(input())
print('{}')
def go(start, cur):
    for i in range(start, n + 1):
        cur.append(i)
        print(*cur)
        go(i + 1, cur)
        cur.pop()
go(1, [])
